set.approach: From the parking area at the Overlook, walk a couple of minutes east along the trail onto the flat top of a rock formation, with the routes below. Take the trail down on the left, or follow the formation right to a steep trail that reaches the base. It is the southernmost line of the streaked vertical wall, immediately right of Dr. Diaper, and follows four bolts to a two-bolt anchor.

review.notes: Area page: trail to the top of the formation and down to the base; route page: position beside Dr. Diaper. No descent stated.

set.approach: Start at the Bald Mountain trailhead and follow the Notch Mountain trail past the Notch Lake turnoffs, staying on the main trail. It crosses three boardwalks, the last a long half-moon-shaped one, then climbs a short rise. At the top of that rise, before the trail bends sharply right, head into the woods straight toward the wall and climb the talus to the start. The route lies on the buttress's far right side, on talus just left of where the lake ends as you come out of the trees.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route from the anchors.

review.notes: Route page gives the right-side approach and rappelling the route; area page gives the trailhead and Notch Mountain trail.

set.approach: Park at Mirror Lake and walk through the woods to reach the small crag. The route follows the corner up to a small roof at the nose.

review.notes: Area page gives the one-line access; route page the line.

set.approach: Drive past the Lower Jungle parking area and around the corner up the road to the marked Upper Jungle pullout. A short approach, marked by cairns, leads down to the crag. Castaway is up and to the left of Climbers in the Mist.

review.notes: Area page: parking and cairned approach; route page: where on the wall. No descent stated.

set.approach: There are two ways in. From the Trial Lake turnoff, park near the dam, cross it heading west and follow the trail north along the lake to Wall Lake, where the upper tier comes into view. Alternatively continue to the Crystal Lake trailhead and take the Wall Lake trail, the first on the right (east), which has better parking. From Wall Lake scramble to the left side, past the main lower tier near the cliff-jumping spot, and cross a short meadow to the climbing. Blue View is right of Prickly Pitch.

review.notes: Area page: two approaches to Wall Lake; route page: neighbour-relative start. No descent stated.
